_note: First counties to watch on election night, in poll-closing order. 'first' says what usually arrives first in that state; it's sourced where a source is given and otherwise marked unverified. Counties are picked for being big, early, or telling. Edit freely.

states.first: The first polls in the country close at 6 PM ET in eastern Kentucky; the western part closes at 7 PM ET. Small eastern counties can report within the hour.
Advance (early in-person) and absentee votes. State law requires counties to report these by 8 PM ET; in 2024 the SOS expected 70-75% of all votes to be in by 8 PM. Election Day precincts follow.
Early and mail votes. Florida law requires counties to report them within 30 minutes of polls closing at 7 PM ET (the Panhandle closes at 8 PM ET). Election Day precincts follow quickly.
Unverified for 2026. Virginia's early and mail votes have often come in as large batches from central absentee precincts. In 2022 they were much more Democratic than Election Day votes.
Unverified: the order varies by county. Assume the first batches can be heavy on early votes.

Town by town, small towns first. New Hampshire has almost no early voting, so partial counts aren't skewed by vote method. They are skewed by geography: small rural towns report before Manchester and Nashua.

Mail ballots that arrived before Election Day come first, then early votes, which counties can't start tabulating until 7:30 PM. Both arrive between about 7:30 and 9:30 PM. Election Day precincts come in between about 8:30 PM and 1 AM.
Early in-person and mail ballots come first, right after polls close at 7:30 PM. Counties can process them for two weeks beforehand. Election Day precincts follow.

Absentees can be pre-processed but not tabulated until polls close. County and clerk sites update before the state's page, which is last. In the 2024 primary, Detroit had more than 80% of its absentees in by 10:30 PM. Four Upper Peninsula counties close at 9 PM ET.

Early vote and mail ballots received so far are released shortly after polls close (8 PM ET in most of the state). In 2020, 88% of Harris County's votes were in that first batch, so the first number is most of the vote. Election Day counts are slow in Harris, Dallas, Tarrant and Collin.
Town by town, through the media. There's no state live feed, and Portland and other big towns take longer.
Unverified. Johnson County's advance votes have usually been an early, large batch.
Unverified for 2026. In 2022, Iowa's early and absentee vote was about D+20 and its Election Day vote about R+26, so whichever comes first will mislead.
Unverified. Rural precincts usually finish before Hennepin and Ramsey.
Most results arrive after 1 AM ET and keep coming for days. Not useful on election night.
